Mr. Justice Rajnesh Oswal, Judge

The petitioner/complainant in WP(Crl) No. 37/2024 (hereinafter to be referred as 'the prosecutrix') is seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 to constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) for investigating the matter or in the alternative for transferring the investigation of the FIR No. 0053 of 2024 registered with Police Station, Bakshi Nagar for commission of offence under Section 376 IPC to Crime Branch or CBI, whereas in the Bail Application, the petitioner/accused, namely, Riyaz Hussain is seeking bail in anticipation of arrest in FIR No. 0053 of 2024 registered with Police Station, Bakshi Nagar for commission of c/w offence under Section 376 IPC, as such, both the petitions have been clubbed together and are taken up together.

2. Issue notice to the respondents for filing response.
3.
Mr. P. D. Singh, learned Dy. AG waives notice on behalf of respondent Nos. 1 to 4.
He shall file response to the writ petition.

sentences.text: 4. Mr. Amit Gupta, Advocate waives notice on behalf of the respondent No. 5.

5. Issue notice to the respondents for filing response.
6.
Mr. P. D. Singh, learned Dy. AG waives notice on behalf of respondent No. 1.
7. Mr. Sandeep Singh, Advocate waives notice on behalf of the respondent No. 2.

8. The prosecutrix has stated that despite registration of FIR, the accused has not been arrested till date, whereas the petitioner/accused, namely, Riyaz Hussain has stated that false and frivolous FIR has been got registered by the respondent No. 2 i.e. the prosecutrix against him.

It is stated by the petitioner/accused that he had approached the court of Presiding Officer, Fast Track, Jammu for seeking bail in anticipation of arrest in the FIR mentioned above, but the same was rejected by the learned court vide order dated 07.05.2024.

entities.text: court of Presiding Officer, Fast Track, Jammu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Besides, it is stated that the petitioner/accused was having a live in relationship with the respondent No. 2 i.e. the prosecutrix, but due to certain issues differences cropped up between them, as a result of which she resorted c/w to blackmail him.
It is also stated that the petitioner/accused used to transfer money in the bank account of the prosecutrix when she was residing with the petitioner.
In order to substantiate the averments made in the bail application, the petitioner/accused has placed on record the account statement and their photographs.

9. A perusal of the FIR reveals that the prosecutrix herself has stated that she had been in physical relations with the petitioner/accused for the last four to five years as the petitioner/accused had made false promise of marriage with her.

It is also alleged that he has also taken Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs.
One Lac) from her during this span of four to five years.

10. Mr. Sandeep Singh, learned counsel for the prosecutrix has submitted that the petitioner/accused has not only sexually assaulted the prosecutrix but also duped her of Rs.
10,00,000/- (Rs. Ten Lacs), though in the FIR due to a typographical error, the amount has been mentioned as Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac).

He has further submitted that the petitioner/accused is not entitled to any concession of bail as he is guilty of committing a heinous offence under Section 376 IPC.
11.

Per contra, Mr. Amit Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused has submitted that photographs placed on record by the petitioner/accused demonstrate that there was close relationship between the petitioner/accused and the prosecutrix and the account statement clearly establishes that the petitioner/accused has paid some amount to the prosecutrix.

12. Heard and perused the record.

sentences.text: contesting parties against each other demonstrate that there were some money transactions between both of them.

The defence projected by the petitioner/accused cannot be termed as imaginary, more particularly, in view of the averments made in the FIR that the prosecutrix was in relationship with the petitioner/accused for the last four to five years, during which they maintained physical relations as well.
14. Prima facie case for indulgence at this stage is made out.
The petitioner deserves to be released on bail.

15. Accordingly, it is provided that till next date of hearing before the Bench, in the event of arrest of petitioner in FIR No. 0053 of 2024 registered with Police Station, Bakshi Nagar for commission of offence under Section 376 IPC, he shall be released on bail, subject to following conditions:
i.

He shall furnish bail bonds with two solvent sureties to the tune of Rs. 50,000/-
each to the satisfaction of Investigating Officer and personal bond of the like amount.
ii. He shall not make any attempt to contact the prosecutrix or any of the prosecution witnesses during bail either physically or through any other mode.
iii. He shall appear before the Investigating Officer from 17.05.2024 to 23.05.2024 from 10.00 AM to 04.00 PM.
c/w iv.
He shall not leave the territory of District, Jammu without prior permission of this Investigating Officer.
16. In the event of violation of any of the conditions mentioned above, the respondents can lay a motion before this Court for cancellation of bail of the applicant/petitioner.
17. Mr. P. D. Singh, learned Dy. AG shall file a detailed status report before the next date of hearing with regard to the compliance of the conditions by the petitioner, imposed by this Court today.

18. List both the petitions on 27.05.2024.
(RAJNESH OSWAL) JUDGE Jammu 15.05.2024
